newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CGT union - hike min wage, halt privatisation.
newsitem.headline: French CGT union - hike min wage, halt privatisation.

text.p: French Communist-led CGT union boss Louis Viannet called on the incoming Socialist-led government on Tuesday to raise the national minimum wage without awaiting the outcome of conference convening the social partners on wages, jobs and work time.
"It will only have meaning if steps are taken very quickly, yes, before conference," he said.
He also said the France Telecom stake sale planned by the outgoing centre-right coalition should be halted and looked at afresh and said all privatisation plans should be suspended.
Asked about his union's stance on France Telecom, Viannet told France Inter radio:
"Let's halt it and re-examine the case. Privatisation of France Telecom has nothing to do with the need to develop the sector and would be bad news for the country's assets".
He also said plans for layoffs at companies should be halted.

Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin, to be prime minister after a left-wing parliamentary election victory on Sunday, has said he will form a government within a week. In the meantime, the outgoing government's privatisation plans remain on the backburner.
Jospin said during the election campaign France Telecom staff would be "consulted" before a decision was taken on the case.
The Socialists' position on privatisations is unclear.

Some political and market analysts believe the party will not ultimately opposes "privatisations" which amount to opening up state companies' capital rather than selling majority control to the private sector.

The Socialists, which want to push for work week of 35 hours instead of 39 plan to call a national jobs and wages conference soon after forming a government to get negotiations going between unions and employers.
